name: Spiced brown nectar
description:
In a saucepan, lightly toast 1 Mexican cinnamon stick, 4 pieces of whole allspice, 3 whole cloves, add 16 oz. of water, steep for about 10 min, extracting all of the flavor; essentially making a tea.

Remove the spices and add 1 cup of piloncillo and 1 cup of dark brown sugar.

On high heat, dissolve the sugar and bring to a boil. Strain nectar and cool it down before use.

This will keep in the refrigerator for up to 1 month.

ingredient_parts.name: Cinnamon
ingredient_parts.description: Cinnamon is a spice derived from the inner bark of trees from the genus Cinnamomum, primarily Ceylon cinnamon (Cinnamomum verum) and cassia cinnamon (Cinnamomum aromaticum). It is commonly used in cooking and baking for its distinct flavor and aroma.

ingredient_parts.name: Clove
ingredient_parts.description: The spice, cloves, is known for its warm, sweet, and aromatic flavor with a hint of spiciness. It has a strong, pungent aroma and is used in both culinary and medicinal applications. Cloves are often used in spice blends, such as pumpkin pie spice and garam masala, and are a key ingredient in many cuisines.

ingredient_parts.name: Allspice
ingredient_parts.description: Allspice berries are the dried, unripe fruit of the *Pimenta dioica* tree, native to the Caribbean and Central America. The name 'allspice' is derived from the fact that the berries possess a complex flavor profile reminiscent of a combination of several spices, including cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, and pepper. They are harvested while still green and allowed to dry, which concentrates their aromatic compounds and creates a robust, intensely fragrant spice. Historically, allspice has been used both as a culinary ingredient and in traditional medicine throughout the regions where it is grown.
